clue.text: My dogs

definitions.note: read as SETTER'S, a possessive, rather than the plural
definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the setter, the person who wrote this puzzle, read with an apostrophe
second meaning: gundogs of a breed such as the Irish or English

explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'my' or 'me' stands for the setter, so 'My' means the setter's; ignore the apostrophe and the same letters name a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword compilers speak of themselves as the setter, and setters are also a family of pointing gundogs.

clue.text: Oval tablet swallowed up by doctor, see

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards
what is swallowed ends up inside the thing that swallows it
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a tablet of medicine is a pill

explanation.surface: A patient's oval pill, prescribed by the doctor, gets swallowed: take a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the one doing the swallowing, but it is the instruction to shuffle 'see', and that shuffled ESE wraps the upturned pill.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is the geometric name for a regular oval shape, so the noun matches the noun.

clue.text: You once include Mike in subject

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: thee is the old form of 'you'
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Someone who used to work with you now includes a man called Mike in their topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word; Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme of a talk or essay is its subject, the topic it is about.

clue.text: Perhaps Shell's about to get penalty, right?

indicators.note: one thing getting another means it gains it, so the next piece is attached after

parts.note: re means 'about' or 'concerning'
a fine is a money penalty
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The oil company Shell is about to be fined, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Shell's' is 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Shell is an oil company that processes crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell is one example of a business that purifies crude oil into fuels, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Tea that's fizzy? It's a ridiculous pretence

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
the ending of fizzy drinks such as lemonade and orangeade

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of sparkling tea as a silly pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: Char (from Chinese cha) is everyday British slang for a cup of tea; a CHAR-ADE would be tea made fizzy like lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd act or pretence that fools nobody, the figurative sense of the parlour game.

clue.text: Cook did stuffing for chicken out of sight

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside a bird, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so the letters that follow are tampered with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A cook made the stuffing for the chicken, then put it somewhere nobody could see.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes 'Cook' a person and 'stuffing' food, but they are the instructions to shuffle and to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hidden is concealed, out of sight of anyone looking for it.

clue.text: Responses to preparing nice roast

indicators.note: preparing food changes it from its raw state, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: How guests respond when the host is cooking a lovely Sunday roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactions are responses to something said or done; both are plural nouns.

clue.text: Tended to send back 75% of puddings after start of dinner

indicators.note: one part coming after another means it is placed following it
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: first letter of dinner

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
three quarters of an eight-letter word leaves six letters, so the last two are dropped

parts.note: puddings are desserts in British usage

explanation.surface: A waiter returned most of the puddings once dinner had begun.
explanation.walkthrough: Three quarters of an eight-letter word drops its last two letters. In Britain 'pudding' is the general word for a sweet course.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse who dressed a wound tended to it, cleaning and bandaging it; both are past tense verbs.

clue.text: Skill of two vessels going around small island

parts.note: the first vessel: a craft is a boat

indicators.note: going around something means surrounding it, so those pieces sit between the two outer ones

parts.note: the second vessel: a ship
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: The skill shown by two boats circling a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: The two vessels are CRAFT and SHIP, placed at either end; the Isle of Man is the crossword's favourite island.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmanship is the skill and quality of work shown by a maker, a near synonym of skill.

clue.text: Republic occasionally rejected suggestion

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the kept letters are read the other way
occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A republic now and then turns down an idea put forward to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint or suggestion pointing towards an answer; here, fittingly, a crossword term.

clue.text: Anger with medic breaking imitations of old dragons

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these pieces go within the last word

parts.note: fakes are imitations

indicators.note: with means alongside, so one piece is set next to the other

parts.note: ire is anger
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An angry doctor smashing replica dragons from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedrake is a fire-breathing dragon of Germanic myth, the plural matching 'old dragons'.

clue.text: Organ observed outside playing Liszt preludes

indicators.note: one word standing outside another wraps around it

parts.note: observed means seen

indicators.note: a prelude is the opening of a piece, so each word gives only its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of playing and Liszt

explanation.surface: An organist was seen performing short Liszt preludes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'Liszt preludes' paint a recital, but the organ is a body part and the preludes take only first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an organ of the body near the stomach that filters blood.

clue.text: National press once grasping English most swiftly?

definitions.note: an adverb for an adjective; the question mark admits the stretch

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: Fleet Street in London, where national newspapers used to be based
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The old newspapers, keen to sign up English writers, went fastest.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street in London was home to the national newspapers until the 1980s and still stands for the press; ST is the usual abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift and nimble, so the fleetest is the quickest of all.

clue.text: Thunberg annoyed after losing right to communicate

indicators.note: one word coming after another is set behind it in order
losing something means it goes missing, so the named letter is taken out

parts.note: Greta Thunberg is the Swedish climate activist
R for right, the letter dropped
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: Greta Thunberg got annoyed after losing an argument about rights she wanted to put over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Thunberg annoyed' as Greta being cross; in fact CROSS follows Greta without her R.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a message across is to make it understood, which is communicating it successfully.

clue.text: Dislikes balconies when end of rung is lowered

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering a letter moves it further down the word, so it is put back in later

parts.note: theatre galleries are upper balconies

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of rung, which is also the first of the balconies word

explanation.surface: People who hate balconies once the bottom rung of the ladder has been let down.
explanation.walkthrough: The G that opens the word for balconies is moved lower down, from the top to the sixth place.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally an allergy to something is a strong dislike of it, as in an allergy to hard work.

clue.text: Discussion with daughter and son over gold

indicators.note: here over means placed after, the two letters following the next piece

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
or is gold in heraldry
D is the abbreviation for daughter
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family talk with the daughter and son about money.
explanation.definitionFit: To have words is to talk things over, often heatedly, so words can mean a discussion.

clue.text: Eccentric lady buying Independent newspaper

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for Independent

explanation.surface: An odd woman buys a copy of The Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is a real British paper, which makes it look like part of the definition; it only supplies the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper published every day of the week.

clue.text: Netflix initially promises to put acting first to get results

indicators.note: the abbreviation for acting is taken from its place and moved to the front
initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of Netflix
to swear is to promise solemnly
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in A/Captain

explanation.surface: Netflix promises to put good acting first to get the viewing figures it wants.
explanation.walkthrough: N and SWEARS give NSWEARS; its A, standing for acting, is lifted out and placed at the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers are the results of solving problems or sums, as in getting the right results.

clue.text: Invitation for Keats: a novel to devour

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
to devour is to eat

explanation.surface: Keats is invited to sit down with a novel to read greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet John Keats and 'a novel' suggest literature; 'novel' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Take a seat' is the polite phrase inviting someone to sit down.

clue.text: Head back into church, uplifted by key spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue something held up by another sits beneath it, so the key letter goes on top

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours Inverness and Sheerness
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A worshipper heads back into church, spirit lifted by the right note.
explanation.walkthrough: A ness is a headland, a common ending in British coastal place names. 'into' simply runs the reversed head on into the church letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract or spirit, as in essence of vanilla.

clue.text: Studio exposed by ultimate lie, regrettably

indicators.note: something exposed by words was there all along, uncovered within them

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An artist's studio is exposed by one final, regrettable lie.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, the French word for a studio.

clue.text: Articles about drink causing disease

indicators.note: about means around, so the articles wrap around the drink

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
gin is a drink
a is the other indefinite article

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles warn that drinking causes illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but it means the grammatical articles AN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is a heart condition causing chest pain, a disease in the broad sense.

clue.text: No one 20 calls for minimal underwear

indicators.note: no means without, so the following item is left out

parts.note: 20 refers to the answer at 20, which means the same as gist
I is the Roman numeral one, the letter dropped
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Nobody rings up asking for skimpy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 down is ESSENCE, and the essence of something is its gist; take out the I and add the calls.
explanation.definitionFit: G-strings are very skimpy thong-style undergarments, minimal underwear indeed.

clue.text: Sun's against religious education being about you!

parts.note: Sol is the sun
V for versus, against

indicators.note: being turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A tabloid complains that faith teaching is all about you.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here it is the Latin Sol. 'you!' is the person doing this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The person reading the clue is the solver of the crossword, so 'you' names them.

clue.text: Lawful escape?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for legitimate or above board

definitions.note: a verb phrase, LEG IT, against the single word
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: British slang for running away

explanation.walkthrough: To leg it is British slang for to run off; the question mark warns of the split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is a clipped informal form of legitimate, meaning legal, and leg it means to flee.

clue.text: Meaning to return number 1 metal? I'd accept iron

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way you went, so everything after is read backwards
to accept something is to take it in, so the iron goes inside

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral one
tin is a metal
taken as written, without the apostrophe
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Asking whether tin really is the top metal: I'd accept iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number 1 metal' reads as one phrase but is three separate pieces; the whole string of wordplay after 'to return' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition states the meaning of a word, and in crosswords it is the part of the clue giving the answer.

clue.text: Network held no protective clothing

indicators.note: having no something means it is missing, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: held tightly
personal protective equipment, the clothing worn for safety

explanation.surface: A workforce was caught without its safety gear.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE, personal protective equipment, became a household abbreviation during the Covid pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines, roads or power cables crossing one another, and also the crossword's own frame.

clue.text: Normal liberal Australia joins America travelling west

indicators.note: in an across clue west is to the left, so the letters are read from right to left
joining things puts them side by side in a row

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
AUS is the abbreviation for Australia
the United States of America

explanation.surface: Business as normal: a liberal Australia allies with a westward-heading America.
explanation.definitionFit: As usual describes what normally happens, the normal state of affairs.

clue.text: Landlord's post

definitions.note: read as LETTER'S, a possessive, rather than the plural
definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to one who lets property, read with an apostrophe

explanation.walkthrough: A landlord lets property, so is a letter; add an apostrophe and that is the landlord's. This matches the trick in 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets out a house is its letter, and the mail through the door is the letters.
